Definition: Ehud, the name of two or three Israelites
BiblicalUsage: Ehud was the left-handed judge from Benjamin whom God raised up to deliver Israel from Eglon, king of Moab. He made a double-edged dagger, hid it under his clothes, and used a private message to reach the king alone in his summer parlour, and after the deed he blew the trumpet and led Israel to take the fords of Jordan. The land had rest for eighty years after him, and the story is told in full in the third chapter of Judges.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe God uses the left-handed, the overlooked, and the unlikely, because Ehud's weakness was the very thing that got him past the guards. I hold that no limitation disqualifies a person God has chosen.
RelatedPeople: Ehud, Son of Gera; Eglon, King of Moab
